findings.reason: the followup must be resolved (or removed) or the plan will send a node to rebuild a landed section.
findings.text: `f-tsigah-067` is `data-status="open"` and recommends `/reckon-build the-suite-is-green-at-head §65`, but s65 is `done` in `plan-section-declarations` (line 27) and its two comments at :1874-1877 record the repair landed at f617b0bd1f with its gate and negative control — so the plan now offers a build command for a section that is already built, and a coordinator reading the open followups would dispatch a redundant node

findings.reason: naming the fix as cache isolation (a fixture that pins `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, which the test does not) rather than an "always builds" invariant would stop the node repairing the wrong layer.
findings.text: s66's success criterion is "a fresh lookup on a fresh store always builds once", but `_store_indexes` (reckon/crew/review_records.py:1493-1507) deliberately starts a process from the index another process persisted for the same store directory, so a store whose resolved path recurs is not fresh and a build is correctly skipped; the criterion therefore cannot distinguish isolating the cache in the fixture from weakening the persisted-index contract the module documents, and a literal reading invites a production change that removes a deliberate optimisation

findings.reason: the plan requires the worker to name the source it measures, so an illustrative cause that is falsified in one run costs a confirmation rather than misleading the repair.
findings.text: the second example cause, "a stat granularity that lets a stale cache match", cannot explain the quoted failure: the failing assertion is the *first* call, where `cached` is `None` and the only route to `len(builds) == 0` is `_load_persisted_entries` accepting a persisted document, and the directory stat identity is consulted only for the in-process cache (`cached[0] == identity`), which coarser granularity would make *more* likely to serve cache, not suppress the first build
